fields.meta_title: Background Check Form for Employers | Emergent
fields.meta_description: What a background check form needs under FTC guidance, plus an app that collects signed authorizations and tracks each candidate's status.
fields.hero_description: A background check form tells a candidate that a report may be ordered and records their written permission. Emergent builds the form and the tracker HR works from.
fields.features_subheading: A PDF gets signed and filed. Emergent's version keeps the signature, the order and the outcome together for each candidate.
fields.feature_1:
The disclosure on a screen of its own

Shows the disclosure with nothing else on the screen, then asks for permission on the next one. Your counsel's wording goes in as written, with no application questions mixed in.
fields.feature_2:
Signatures from any phone

Captures a typed or drawn signature and stamps it with the date and time. Each signed authorization lands on the candidate's record, beside the role and the recruiter who asked.
fields.feature_3:
Hand-off to your screening provider

Passes the candidate's details to the screening company you already use through its API once the form is signed. Results return to that same record, and nobody retypes a birth date.
fields.feature_4:
A status for every person

Lists who has signed, who is waiting on a result and who has not opened the link. Email reminders go out on the schedule you pick and stop the moment a signature comes in.
fields.feature_5:
Notices that follow a bad result

Writes the pre-adverse action notice and attaches the report plus the summary of rights. The decision waits the number of days your policy sets, then the second notice goes out.
fields.feature_6:
An app you can take with you

Exports the whole codebase to your GitHub repository. Your engineers can host it themselves or wire it into the applicant tracking system you run, or ask Emergent to build that sync.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places a Background Check Starts
fields.tab_content_1:
Signed in a truck cab while the recruiter waits

Drivers apply from the cab, not a desk. A Northwind Freight candidate opens the link on his phone and reads the disclosure on a screen that holds nothing else. He signs the authorization on the next screen. Priya Nair in HR sees the signed packet on his record at 4:12 PM, and the order goes to the screening provider.
fields.tab_content_2:
31 of 38 coaches signed before the first practice

Volunteer seasons start on a deadline. Riverside Youth Soccer needs every volunteer coach signed before the first practice, and 7 are still out. Each one gets an email reminder every three days, and the league secretary watches the count fall without making a call.
fields.tab_content_3:
Five business days between the notice and the decision

A report with a conviction on it does not end the process. For a Northwind warehouse applicant, the app drafts the pre-adverse action notice with a copy of the report and the FCRA rights summary attached. The decision waits 5 business days, the window HR chose, before the final notice can go out.
fields.tab_content_4:
Badges at the hospital wait on each clearance

Client sites set their own rules. Globex Facilities sends 12 HVAC technicians to a hospital that badges only cleared contractors. The vendor coordinator sees 9 of 12 cleared, 2 waiting on a result and 1 who has not signed. That technician gets the link again by email, and the hospital's badge office receives the cleared list.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Background Check Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps written for the employer: what the form asks, what stays off it, and what to do when a report comes back.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask only for what the provider needs
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Match the checks to the role
fields.howto_step_1_des: Give the disclosure its own document or screen. FTC guidance says it must stand alone and cannot sit inside a job application. Keep it short and plain, and leave out waivers and policy text that would compete with it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for a signature on the authorization before any report is ordered. Current employees sign one too when you check them. Record the date of each signature, because that date is what you point to if anyone asks when consent was given.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Collect the legal name, any former names, date of birth and the address history your provider asks for. Keep the Social Security number in a field only HR can open, and skip any question the role does not require.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Scope each check to the job: a driving record for drivers, credit history only where someone handles money. Apply one standard to every applicant for that role, as FTC and EEOC guidance both expect.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give each candidate a status: link sent, signed, ordered, result in. Remind anyone who has not signed after a few days. A list of statuses tells the recruiter which offers can move today and which are waiting on paperwork.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before acting on a report, send a notice with a copy of it and the FCRA summary of rights, then wait the period your policy sets. The final notice names the reporting company and explains the right to dispute what it found.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Store reports away from the general personnel file and agree a retention period with counsel. When it ends, delete the electronic copies in a way that leaves them unreadable, as the FTC's disposal guidance describes for employers.

plan.angle: The top results are agency PDFs (state police, townships, a university system) and one template page: each is a paper slip that someone signs and someone else files. Searchers want the employer's authorization form. This page says what the form must carry under FTC guidance (a disclosure on its own, written permission), what to leave off, and then builds what a PDF cannot: the signature on a phone, status per person, the hand-off to the screening provider, and the notices that follow a bad result.

claims_to_source: Employers must tell the applicant in writing, in a stand-alone document that is not part of the job application, that a background report may be used, and get written permission before the check

Before an adverse action based on the report, the employer gives a notice with a copy of the report and A Summary of Your Rights Under the FCRA; after it, a notice naming the reporting company and the right to dispute and get a free report within 60 days
Employers must apply the same background check standards to everyone regardless of race, national origin, sex, religion, disability or age, and dispose of reports securely
Consumer reports may not include arrest records older than seven years, except for jobs paying $75,000 or more a year
ATF Form 4473 is the firearms transaction record a licensed dealer completes with the buyer, and the dealer runs a NICS background check before the transfer
Anyone can request their own FBI Identity History Summary, with fingerprints and an $18 fee

Nationwide specialty consumer reporting agencies, including employment screening companies, give a free file disclosure every 12 months on request; employers need written permission before running an employment report
